1. (Currently amended) A control system comprising: a controller including a processor and memory, the controller configured to be communicatively coupled to automation components in the control system and to facilitate performance of a process through interoperation with the automation components by generating a holistic state data, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data by: determining a model configured to describe the process used by the controller; determining input and output variables of the process; determining constraints on the input and output variables; determining an objective function associated with the process used by the controller; and storing the model, the input and output variables, the constraints, and the objective function in one of a plurality of fields in the holistic state data to enable the automation components to detect and operate with the controller upon receiving the holistic state data, wherein the holistic state data is used by the automation components to automatically adjust operational parameters of the automation components based on the model, input and output variables, and constraints.

2. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to be communicatively coupled to the automation components via a communication network and to communicate the holistic state data to each of the automation components upon connecting to the communication network, wherein the automation components use the holistic state data to synchronize their operational states with the controller.

3. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to be communicatively coupled to the automation components via a backplane and to communicate the holistic state data to the automation components upon connecting to the backplane, wherein the backplane facilitates direct hardware-level communication of the holistic state data.

4. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the holistic state data is a standardized format understood by each of the automation components, and wherein the standardized format includes predefined fields for the model, input and output variables, constraints, and objective function.

5. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data by: determining an intermediate search result of an optimization search; determining a state of the optimization search when the intermediate search result is determined; and storing the intermediate search result and the state in an optimization state field of the holistic state data, wherein the optimization state field enables resumption of the optimization search by the automation components.

6. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data to facilitate performing an optimization search in conjunction with one or more of the automation components in the control system, wherein the optimization search adjusts the input and output variables to optimize the objective function.

7. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data by: determining computational capabilities of the controller; determining interconnections with the automation components in the control system; and storing the computational capabilities and the interconnections in a controller settings field of the holistic state data, wherein the automation components use the controller settings field to determine task allocation.

8. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to communicate the holistic state data to a server in the control system to facilitate determining an optimization problem, wherein the server uses the holistic state data to formulate the optimization problem based on the model and constraints.

9. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller comprises an in-memory database configured to store the holistic state data, wherein the in-memory database provides rapid access to the holistic state data for the automation components.

10. (Currently amended) A tangible, non-transitory computer-readable medium configured to store instructions executable by a processor of a controller, wherein the instructions comprise instructions to: receive, using the processor, control system configuration data; determine, using the processor, automation components communicatively coupled to the controller and characteristics of the automation components based at least in part on the control system configuration data; determine, using the processor, an optimization problem based at least in part on the automation components and the characteristics of each of the automation components, wherein the optimization problem includes constraints and an objective function derived from the characteristics; and instruct, using the processor, one or more of the automation components to perform a control action in a process, wherein the control action is determined based at least in part on solving the optimization problem, and wherein the control action directly modifies physical parameters of the process.

11. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the characteristics of each of the automation components comprise a model used by the automation component, wherein the instructions to determine the optimization problem comprise instructions to determine the optimization problem based at least in part on the model used by each of the automation components, and wherein the model describes the relationship between inputs and outputs of the automation component.

12. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the characteristics of each of the automation components comprise a computing capability of the automation component, wherein the instructions to determine the optimization problem comprise instructions to determine the optimization problem based at least in part on computing compatibilities of each of the automation components, and wherein the computing capability limits the complexity of the optimization problem.

13. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the control system configuration data comprises a plurality of holistic state data, wherein each of the plurality of holistic state data corresponds with one of the automation components, and wherein each holistic state data includes the model, input and output variables, and constraints for the corresponding automation component.

14. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 13, wherein the instructions to determine the automation components and characteristics of the automation components comprise instructions to parse each of the plurality of holistic state data to extract the model, input and output variables, and constraints.

15. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 13, wherein each of the plurality of holistic state data comprises a standardized format with same fields, wherein the same fields include a model field, a variables field, a constraints field, and an objective function field.

16. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the instructions to receive the configuration data comprise instructions to receive the configuration data from a cloud, wherein the cloud stores the control system configuration data and provides the configuration data to the controller via a network connection.

17. (Currently amended) A method for performing diagnostics on a control system comprising: determining, using a processor, holistic state data captured by a controller in the control system; simulating, using the processor, operation of the controller based at least in part on the holistic state data while the controller performs other operations, wherein the simulation uses a model and constraints stored in the holistic state data; analyzing, using the processor, the simulation of the controller to perform diagnostics on the controller, wherein the analysis compares simulated results with actual results; adjusting, using the processor, operation of the control system based at least in part on the diagnostics, wherein the adjustment modifies parameters of the controller or automation components.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, wherein: simulating operation comprises simulating performance of various control actions by the controller; and analyzing the simulation comprises analyzing results of the various control actions to determine which control actions achieve the objective function.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, wherein analyzing the simulation comprises: determining a predicted response to a control action determined by the controller using a model stored in the holistic state data; and comparing the predicted result with an actual response to the control action to determine accuracy of the model, wherein the comparison identifies deviations between predicted and actual responses.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 19, comprising adjusting the model when the predicted response and the actual response vary, wherein the adjusted model is stored in the holistic state data for use in subsequent control actions.
